summary: Iteration 16 tested the new catch popup (CatchCard) and fish length. Backend: 7 of 8 pytest checks passed. The land response includes length_cm, which equals fish_length(species, weight). Every inventory fish has a consistent length_cm, so the backfill worked. Sell pays the vendor price and removes the fish from inventory. Bluegill weighing 0.1-0.9 kg measures 15.3-31.8 cm, and pike is about 1.5x longer than carp at the same weight. The one failure is a keyword bug in fish_size.py (see backend_issues). Frontend: as TestAngler on Millbrook, the player was teleported onto spot fish-1 by setting window.__fx.me, then a real cast was made with Space. The test then intercepted POST /fish/land and changed it to success=true after the stamina wait. Everything else is real server data. Six fish were landed in the UI: Warmouth (uncommon, 35 cm), Brown Bullhead, Mirror Carp, Old Millbrook Bass (epic, 3 stars), Grass Carp, and Escaped Koi (rare, 3 stars, NEW SPECIES line shown). The popup renders correctly: catch-name 'X CAUGHT!', underwater scene, rarity chip, measuring tape with the length at its end, length/weight, data-stars matching the rarity (uncommon 2, rare 3), 'You've gained N exp', worth/Sell price. All images load (naturalWidth > 0). Keep closes the popup and the fish stays in inventory. Sell closes the popup, shows the toast 'Sold for 773 gold', gold goes from 6080 to 6853, and the fish is removed. VIEW IN FISHDEX closes the popup and goes to /game/journal, where the Fishdex opens. The X close button is partly covered by the title (see ui_bugs). At 1920x800 nothing overflows the viewport. Regression: the willow mapcheck audit lists are all empty with spawn=true, and Crew Island requests crew_island.mp3.

minor.issue: Shape keywords are matched as plain substrings, so some fish get the wrong body shape. 'Green Moray' and 'Cinderjaw Moray' contain 'ray' and get the DEEP shape (a=0.028): 30 kg gives 102 cm, but a real moray of that weight is about 2.5 m (it should use EEL). 'Grayling' contains 'ray' and is treated as deep-bodied. 'Bluntnose Sixgill' (a shark) contains 'gill' and is treated as deep-bodied: 600 kg gives 278 cm, about half its real length. 'Giant Snakehead' contains 'snake' and gets the EEL shape: 20 kg gives 223 cm, but real is about 120 cm. 'Crayfish Eater' also matches 'ray'. Fix: check whole words or apply exclusions (moray -> EEL before DEEP; skip ray inside grayling/crayfish; sixgill -> default; snakehead -> SLENDER). Deep-bodied sunfish-family species without a keyword (Warmouth: 0.55 kg gives 34.8 cm, real max about 31 cm) and bass (Old Millbrook Bass: 6.8 kg gives 80 cm, real about 65-70 cm) come out somewhat long under the default a=0.013. Consider adding 'warmouth', 'bass' (a about 0.016), and others.

Some map tile assets intermittently returned HTTP 503 (fountain.webp, t_grass.webp, t_snow.webp). Once this raised the Emergent 'Unhandled rejection' overlay from the Pixi Loader.load, which blocked the UI. The 503s are probably preview-infra or a burst of prewarm requests. Pixi texture loads still need a catch/retry so one failed asset cannot cause an unhandled rejection.

ui_bugs.issue: The title div (catch-name, class gold-text) has a CSS filter, which creates a stacking context. It is also rendered after the absolutely positioned X button, so it paints on top of most of the X. elementFromPoint at the X centre, top and lower-left all return catch-name. Only the bottom-right corner reaches the button. A normal Playwright click on catch-close-btn timed out ('catch-name intercepts pointer events'), and real users clicking the middle of the X will hit nothing. Fix: add z-10 (or relative z-20) to the close button, or render it after the title.

issues: The card renders only about 258 px wide. Cause: CatchCard sits inside the scaled game-hud (transform: scale(s)), and max-w-[94vw] is in viewport units, so it shrinks again by s. Use max-w-[94%] or a width based on the HUD's w/s.

Because the card is so narrow, the right column wraps: 'You've gained' is on 2 lines, '74 exp' is on 2 lines, and 'worth 180 g' wraps. The Sell button wraps to 'Sell / 129 g' and is taller than Keep. The VIEW IN FISHDEX text is two lines in a small green pill. The stars are 53 px wide in total. The tape numbers 1-5 and the end value are still readable and nothing overflows.

'VIEW IN FISHDEX' wraps to two lines: the span is 50 px tall in a 44-50 px button and 'FISHDEX' sits on the lower edge of the green button art. Add whitespace-nowrap or smaller text, or widen the button.
The fish art is generic and based on rarity (for example lagoon_carp.png, a golden carp, was shown for Warmouth). That is acceptable with the current art set but does not depict the species.

action_items: Put the CatchCard close button above the title (z-10, or move it after the title) so the X is clickable.
Change CatchCard max-w-[94vw] to max-w-[94%] (it sits in the scaled HUD) so the popup is not tiny on mobile, and prevent the Sell and VIEW IN FISHDEX labels from wrapping.
Fix the fish_size keyword matching: moray -> eel; grayling, crayfish, sixgill and snakehead are misclassified. Optionally tune the default shape for bass/warmouth.
Make Pixi asset loading resilient to an occasional 503 (catch/retry) so the unhandled-rejection overlay cannot appear.
critical_code_review_comments: CatchCard: the X button has no z-index and the title, which has a filter (and therefore a stacking context), is rendered after it, so the title covers the button.
CatchCard: viewport units (94vw) inside a transform-scaled container shrink twice.

Sell button label uses c.vendor ?? value*0.7, but the land response has no vendor field, so it always falls back to 70% of value. The actual payout comes from vendor_quotes (gear/perks), so the label can differ from what is paid. The sold Old Millbrook Bass paid 773 g. Consider returning the vendor quote in the land response.
fish_size: matching on substrings is fragile; match on word tokens.

success_rate.frontend: 85% (popup content, Keep, Sell, Fishdex, regression pass; the X click is blocked by the overlapping title, and the mobile sizing is off)

test_credentials: TestAngler / Angler#2026 (the login response key is 'token', not access_token)
seed_data_creation: About 8 catches landed for TestAngler on Millbrook. Some were kept and others sold, and gold went up.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Fast UI catch flow: put the token in localStorage owo_token, set sessionStorage fr_mode='water', open /game (TestAngler is on Millbrook). Then run __fx.path=[]; __fx.dest=null; __fx.me.x=1506; __fx.me.y=1047 to stand on spot fish-1. Wait until __fx.phase==='idle' && __fx.atSpot, then press Space. Intercept **/api/fish/land with page.route: wait stamina*0.95+0.5 s after the cast response, then continue with success=true, elapsed/game_time=stamina*0.95 and holds [[i, i+0.6]]. The catch-popup appears within about 20 s. Use JS click for catch-close-btn until the z-index bug is fixed.
rca of the issue: X not clickable: .gold-text has filter: drop-shadow, which makes the title a stacking context painted after the earlier absolutely positioned button (the button has no z-index), so the title's box covers the lower and middle part of the 40 px X. Mobile tiny popup: World.js renders CatchCard inside game-hud with transform scale(s) and width w/s, and the card's max-w-[94vw] resolves against the real viewport, so the final width is 94vw*s.
